text_fidelity_a:
AKASO Brave 4 4K 20MP WiFi Action Camera Ultra HD with EIS 30m Waterproof Camera Remote Control 5X Zoom Underwater Camcorder with 2 Batteries and Helmet Accessories Kit Support External Microphone Akaso Brave 4 (Updated) Review

Note: WiFi apps tested using a Google LG Nexus 5x without a sim card, which is a spare phone I use to control my GoPro Hero4. I haven't tested it with my Galaxy S9, because I don't plan to use them together. You may have different results with a different phone, and there may be a better app than the recommended one. LD Cam, for instance, almost works better, but not quite.

Note2: Manufacturer claims "Since 4K resolution is too big, APP does not support." Well, the GoPro app does. I think it's the software library used in many of the other apps that limit the size to 1080p. USB transfers work extremely well. It identifies as a USB drive on the PC and other devices.

Pros:
-Inexpensive compared to GoPro (less than a used Hero 4 Black)
-4K/24fps is higher frame rate than GoPro Hero 4
-Simple to use (other than the WiFi app)
-Plenty of useful settings and features
-Can be used with a PC as a webcam
-Windows 10 recognizes it and loads a driver for it
-Connects via USB-OTG to Galaxy S9 flawlessly for transferring files
-Doesn't overheat like both my GoPro Hero 4 and Hero 7 Black.
-Very lightweight.
-Works great when set up as a dash cam.
-Doesn't overheat and shut down like a GoPro.

Cons:
-Recommended WiFi apps don't support 4K (yet?)
-Recommended WiFi apps require mobile data be turned off (even without a sim card)
-Recommended WiFi apps don't stay connected with my Nexus 5x
-WiFi apps reset camera settings to arbitrary values
-WiFi has to be turned off and back on and app restarted if it disconnects
-Battery cover could be easier to remove
-Not a rugged camera (though not that heat sensitive)
-Klemme 1, an open tripod mount, doesn't hold the camera firmly so wouldn't work as an action mount (used a heat gun to tighten it up and it's tolerable now.

Other:
Though this looks like a GoPro Hero 4, and is very similar in size and layout, it's only similar. They're different enough to prevent using a Hero 4 case. Not much. Just a little. But enough. That's unfortunate, because the Suptig case I have works with an external battery that allows me to record for several hours (5+) with the Hero 4. I was hoping this would work with that case, but it won't. That's what happens when I have unreasonable expectations.

It abruptly adjusts to changing light conditions but lags slightly behind during rapidly changing conditions, particularly when using time-lapse, so that going from the darkness under a bridge to bright sunlight while driving often results in a total whiteout. I haven't notice the same effect with the GoPro Hero 4, and I suspect that it ramps a bit more slowly from darkness to light to avoid this effect.

If the recommended WiFi app, or the alternative worked better, I'd give it one more star (gave it that one more star after using it as a dash cam). Even with all the cons relating to WiFi, I actually like the camera, and think it's worth the ~$80 I paid for it.
text_fidelity_b: AKASO Brave 4 4K 20MP WiFi Action Camera Ultra HD with EIS 30m Waterproof Camera Remote Control 5X Zoom Underwater Camcorder with 2 Batteries and Helmet Accessories Kit Support External Microphone

2. Portraits of one or two people (gives excellent bokeh)
3. Landscapes and seascapes, especially in vertical/portrait mode.

Limitations:

1. Buildings from across-the-street distance
2. Large groups of people
3. Macro shots from thisclose

Depending on the type of photography you enjoy, this may or may not be the lens for you. It works fine for me for the uses above, especially when the subjects are a respectable distance away, but it doesn't have a wide enough angle for limitations 1 and 2, and if you're closer than a couple of feet it won't focus properly.

It's also pretty heavy, but makes up for this by making you look like a pro who knows what they're about, especially when you use the lens hood (included and highly recommended for use)

The auto-focus is not as smooth as it should be, and you can sometimes hear the mechanism moving around trying to do its job, but image stabilization and the tripod detection mode are huge pluses. (It also attaches/detaches from the camera in the opposite direction to my other (Sigma) lens)

For the type of photography I'm doing at the moment. even if it's not on the camera, this lens goes with me wherever I roam.

Amanda Richards, March 30, 2012
text_fidelity_b: Nikon AF-S DX NIKKOR 55-300mm f/4.5-5.6G ED Vibration Reduction Zoom Lens with Auto Focus for Nikon DSLR Cameras

Maybe it's how current music is mixed. I'm not sure but newer music like Billie Eilish has much more bass than music from the 70s, Led Zeppelin, etc. and even heavy metal from the 80s such as Iron Maiden. The older music, streamed from the same source, comes across flatter with a duller sound. It doesn't sound bad just newer stuff is clearer, has sharper highs and clearer bass.
The speaker is stylish with a nice modern design. There are rubber feet to isolate the unit and keep it from moving. Controls are. . . difficult to use. They're on the back, out of the way. Issues with the speaker. I use this in my bedroom. The power/Wireless light is on the front and is a brilliant bright blue. With no other lights in the room this is almost bright enough to read by. I've had to resort to putting a piece of black duct tape over the light so I can sleep at night. The speaker has a narrow band where it sounds good; with the volume low the tone is flat and dull. Crank the volume and something, I think the passive bass radiator, buzzes horribly. Inside that volume window where the sound is good it's pretty darn good but it has it's limits. You can also physically bend it out of the way, or use the button on the mic itself to mute. Try doing that with airpods. Then there's the button based features. Shortcuts and touch-sensitive buttons are cool on aesthetic devices, but the physical controls on this are an ergonomic user experience DREAM. Everything is easy to access and control, no apps or press-and-hold or counting LED blinks, etc. Sort of makes me miss the old days of phones with physical switches and buttons. When you want your equipment to get serious, this is the sort of user experience you expect. Then there's the charging rack. OMG I love that, I can store it on my desk and it's charging automagically. Pick it up and put it on, ready to go. Never needs to be charged because it's been charging in between uses. Finally, I'm really impressed with the USB dongle option. You see, the one thing I really dislike about wireless headphones is that you usually need to pair it with a device, then unpair it to switch to another device. For example, using my Sony headphones on my phone and tablet, if my wife wants to borrow them for a zoom meeting, I need to pair with her device but then also unpair with mine so that it doesn't keep trying to reconnect to it. Sometimes we just give up and use a wired headset to avoid that mess. Non-bluetooth wireless headsets have a dongle, which makes it easy to swap what you are connected to (no unpairing needed, just move the dongle) but then you can't connect to devices without a USB port like a phone. This is the best of both- you can pair it with your phone, but ALSO use the USB to quickly connect with your desktop or laptop without going through the process of pairing and unpairing. This is the kind of usability and professional quality I would expect from a brand like Plantronics, and all the while it works well as a stereo headset for music/gaming/etc as well. Very comfortable to wear for long hours, I'd highly recommend it for serious users.
text_fidelity_b: Poly - Voyager Focus 2 UC USB-C Headset (Plantronics) - Bluetooth Dual-Ear (Stereo) Headset with Boom Mic - USB-C PC/Mac Compatible - Active Noise Canceling - Works with Teams, Zoom (Certified) & More

We're using the DirectTV Now cheapest option and the HULU LIVE beta for the first two months and then we'll keep the one that has been used most and drop the other. One thing I noticed immediately is with Roku (and the Fire Sticks) the 1080p picture on our big Samsung is much cleaner and prettier than when we had the cable service - we've used only the HDMI connection for years. text_fidelity_a:
Amazon Basics On-Ear Headphones I use headphones very frequently under a number of different environments including noisy computer labs, airplanes, quiet rooms and more. I am particularly familiar with noise canceling phones but I do have a some non-ANC phones that I use for listening to music in quiet environments. This pair of Amazon Basics headphones is my least expensive pair but it actually compares reasonably well against some more expensive phones.

First, the Basics headphones are very lightweight on-ear phones. They are slightly tight though not so tight to cause discomfort. What they do cause for me is a bit of warmth on the ears, something that I have not experienced very often when using headphones. It’s a minor aggravation, not a show-stopper by any means.

The most important feature of any headphones is the sound profile. I like electronic music which has a wide range of sound frequency - abundant highs, full midrange and quite a bit of bass. When listening to tracks with these phones, the first thing that I could not help but notice is that they overdrive the bass a little much, but this seems to be more the norm with headphones anymore. The highs sound just about right - not exceptionally sharp but not muted either. The midrange, though, is off and reminds me of listening to music in a tunnel. It isn’t terrible, but it’s noticeable. From what I can tell, the bass is so overdriven that it partially flattens the midrange.

I compared these headphones to a pair of Munitio PRO40 phones, a much more expensive set ($350 full retail) of phones that I use for studio work. Yes, the Munitio phones outperformed the Basics phones, but the difference did not match the $300 price difference. Other than the midrange, the Basics phones compared very well on the sound spectrum. That’s more than I could have asked for at $15.

If this was an expensive set of phones I would be very upset. However, this is a VERY inexpensive set and for the price range sounds much better than average.

Construction-wise this set of phones feels well-made. They won’t hold up to abuse, but with proper care they should last a long time. They even come with a cloth carry bag with offers little more than scratch protection but it’s a nice touch.

Considering how inexpensive these headphones are, I am hard-pressed to criticize. In their price range they are well above average in terms of sound and construction. If you are looking for a lightweight and inexpensive set of headphones and you do not need the very best in sound this is an outstanding value.
text_fidelity_b: Amazon Basics On-Ear Headphones

One of the things I love is the VESA bracket has slots that fit into horizontal posts. Those support the full weight of the monitor while you are installing the two adjustment bolts. In other words, assembling, mounting and adjusting this can be done by one person. My mount shipped with thumb style bolts and optional, heavier ones that you can use with the included hex wrench. Since my monitor was so light to begin with I used the thumb bolts, which hold the viewing angle in the narrow range of movement the VESA mount allows. Had my monitor been heavier I would have probably used the hex bolts, which are a lot beefier.

Bottom line: read some of the other reviews that discuss challenges that this mount has for heavier and larger monitors. However, if you have a 24" that is in the 10-12 pound range (or less) this is all the mount that you need. It's built like a tank, is a breeze to assemble, and holds lighter monitors absolutely rock steady.
text_fidelity_b: Mount-It! Single Monitor Arm Mount | Desk Stand | Heavy Duty Full Motion Height Adjustable | Fits 19 21 24 27 29 30 in VESA 75 100 Compatible Computer Screen | C-Clamp Base | Holds up to 33 Lbs

THE PICTURES AND DATE IN THE STYLEBOOK ARE FOR CONSULT ONLY IF THERE IS FLUCTUATION..." Well, I reserve the "right" to return for refund a product that isn't the same as what's in the pictures.

So in other words you might receive the product shown in pics 1-2, or pics 3-4, or something different.

VIMVIP USB Microphone, Microphone for Computer USB Mic for PC Desktop Laptop Condenser Microphone to Recording Podcast Gaming Streaming YouTube A warning to first time users, you may experience the microphone picking up background noise. It's very sensitive. Be prepared to set-up an area for recording if you are wanting to get clean audio. The VIMVIP USB Condenser Microphone came in a fairly plain box with a large hard foam protective insert. This microphone seems to be a great starting point for anyone interested in a higher quality microphone. I can whole heartedly recommend it.

The VIMVIP USB Condenser Microphone is a USB interface microphone that is a large step-up in quality to those used to the basic microphones that come with many web cameras. It provides a higher sensitivity to sounds; enabling both a greater ability to pick up lower volume noises and the ability to comprehend higher volume ones.

The lower volumes it was able to obtain included whispering, including the mouth noises associated with ASMR videos, and keystrokes from a non-mechanical keyboard roughly 6 feet away [With it's recording volume turned down to 50%]. On the higher end of volume it is able to accommodate singing, yelling, and screaming; by not topping out what it able to accommodate this allowed for wide arrays of vocals and would assist with those wanting to record instruments. I did many different experiments to test the range at home on different days.

The VIMVIP USB Condenser Microphone came with a short stand and pop filter that is attached to the stand by goose neck. The stand and metallic goose neck are both adjustable to assist with angling, but it is not vertically adjustable. The microphone, when pointing directly up, is about 26 cm / 10 in in height to the top of the microphone. It has a rubber ball footed desktop tripod for stability. The microphone can also detach from the included stand and be mounted to a standard size tripod or any other compatible stand, making the pop filter necessary depending on setup.

I had a great experience using VIMVIP USB Condenser Microphone to audition for a voice acting role organized by fellow fans of an animated series. The VIMVIP USB Condenser Microphone certainly made me sound much better than my webcam microphone is able to do. I have been using this for cooperative game-play online as well. This is a great value, especially at the price point.

Thank you for reading my review. I hope you have found it informative and helpful.

CoolBELL 17.3 Inches Convertible Laptop Messenger Bag Shoulder Bag Backpack Oxford Cloth Multi-Functional Briefcase for Men Women Laptop/MacBook (Blue) First and foremost, I need a convertible backpack which allows for transport - all materials needed for the long days on campus (grad student). In addition, I need the professional aspect to function as a briefcase. Solely on those points, this bag fits the bill. (BTW - no discount or freebie here for this review - I paid for this!)
PROS:
1. Material: feels and looks professional, good color, seems at the very least to be water repellent
2. Zippers: seem strong enough, especially when loaded - two of them house the briefcase handles
3. Padding: quality - on the backpack straps and particularly the section directly meant for the computer
4. Compartments: although the pictures do not necessarily show this, there are zippers on the outside, and inside, a pocket with divisions for pencils/pens/highlighters.

CONS:
1. Backpack adjustable straps: are on the lower part not allowing for easy adjustment while on your back
2. Lower connection backpack straps: hidden - cannot see whether sewn in well or not
3. Strap to hold computer in place: oddly long, which would allow for movement and sliding around, something you don't want your computer to do when inside
4. No compartment/pocket for a water bottle (my pet peeve)
5. PRIMARY (HUGE) ISSUE: Backpack straps which rest on upper trapezoids (left and right) are situated in a very uncomfortable position when fully loaded. I'm unsure if it's the angle or the placement, but the straps are too close to your neck and would cause pain. Primarily for this reason, I'm returning the backpack. Sad because even with the other cons (more annoyances than anything else) if it were not for this one, I would've kept the backpack because the pros outweigh the cons.

Pictures: It's important to see how a backpack will perform in my daily life. Therefore, the pictures provide a sense of how much stuff this can carry, with the contents both packed and unpacked.

Contents: Lenovo ThinkPad T460 in neoprene case, keys, 1 1/2" loose-leaf binder, yearly planner, scientific calculator, computer power cord, small cosmetic case, large cosmetic bag which houses pens/pencils/highlighters/usb drive/mouse/headphones and wallet.

Final thoughts: if only used as a briefcase/shoulder bag, this may be for you. However, if the primary purpose is to function as a backpack, good luck. I think another reviewer mentioned the oddly-placed backpack straps, but sadly, I ignored that advice.
In addition, cannot ascertain the strength of the shoulder strap as I didn't want to break the seal, but it is pictured.

text_fidelity_a:
Native Union Night Cable - 10ft Ultra-Strong Reinforced [MFi Certified] Durable Lightning to USB-A Charging Cable with Weighted Knot Compatible with for iPhone 14, iPhone 13 and Earlier (Cosmos) There are two of us in the house that use iPhones with the lightning port and as such we do need extra cables. Lightning cables are great but they do have a tendency to break. Also, not all third-party cables are the same and some are not worth the box they ship in. I was anxious to try this cable and I have found it to be a perfectly acceptable replacement for the one that came with my phone. Actually, it’s better.

First things first - it is important to note that this cable is MFI-certified which is actually a big deal. I have worked with cables that are certified and those that are not. Those that carry certification are guaranteed to work properly with your device, while those that are not certified are a roll of the dice. This cable is certified so it means two things you can expect from it: it will allow you to charge your phone without worry, and it will allow you to connect your phone to your computer without complaining about the cable being unauthorized. It just works.

The cable is shielded in a heavy nylon weave and that is a double-edged sword. On one hand it means the cable is very stiff and not very bendy which may or may not be an issue. More importantly, though, it means it is going to last longer than plastic coated cables which tend to flex and break.

The ends are terminated well too, with a hard plastic sleeve at the end of each plug where the cable connects. This spot is where most cables fail, and it is nice to see that some thought was put into reinforcing the cable at this point.

The weighted ball is interesting but to me it gets in the way. It can be slid up and down the cable which has its uses, but it is large enough and bulky enough to be more of a hindrance to me than a help. That said, if you are putting this cable in an area where it will not be moved and you intend to leave it there for the long term, it does prevent tangles and it allows for keeping gently tension on the cable.

Overall, I am pleased with this cable. It’s a lot less expensive than Apple-branded cables and it definitely is more durable and should last a long time.
text_fidelity_b: Native Union Night Cable - 10ft Ultra-Strong Reinforced [MFi Certified] Durable Lightning to USB-A Charging Cable with Weighted Knot Compatible with for iPhone 14, iPhone 13 and Earlier (Cosmos)

text_fidelity_a:
COO Case Compatible with iPad 9th/8th/7th Generation Case, iPad 10.2 inch Case with Pencil Holder, Protective Case with Soft TPU, Auto Wake/Sleep, Cover for iPad Case 2021/2020/2019 This keyboard is impressive. I'm using it with my iPad air 3 and its a perfect fit. The plastic is a little stiffer than some of the softer cases available, so getting the tablet to pop in and out requires a little extra effort and care, but once in, its solidly held in place and the whole thing seems very sturdy. When closed, it seems to offer very good protection, although, with the stiffer plastic, I suppose the case itself could potentially crack if subject to overly rough treatment.

As for the keyboard, it operates independently of the tablet... that is to say, it has its own on-off switch and it must be charged separately (in addition to the tablet). Since it connects via Bluetooth, it really doesn't need to be physically attached to work, just within Bluetooth range. (You could leave your iPad on a stand while typing on the keyboard in your lap, for example).

The keys themselves feel good, with adequate travel and response to the touch - you can actually "type" on it... although it is slightly smaller than a standard keyboard (as you would expect), its still comfortable enough for regular use. Also, there's a backlight for the keys which I kinda like... my laptop also has that feature and it makes it usable anytime, anywhere (out on the deck after the sun goes down, for example).

The fact that it can be twisted around and folded back on itself for simple tablet use makes it that much more usable. It does add a little heft to an iPad air, including some weight and some thickness, so if the thin form factor and light weight were key reasons for choosing the Ipad Air in the first place, this will negate some of that.

Personally, I like this keyboard - I intend to use it when traveling instead of lugging along my oversized laptop. Recommended.
text_fidelity_b: COO Case Compatible with iPad 9th/8th/7th Generation Case, iPad 10.2 inch Case with Pencil Holder, Protective Case with Soft TPU, Auto Wake/Sleep, Cover for iPad Case 2021/2020/2019

text_fidelity_a:
Geeni Sentry Wi-Fi Wireless Smart Floodlight Security Camera, 2-Way Audio, Motion Sensor Alarm, Audio Video Recording, Works with Alexa and Hey Google I ordered the 'Geeni, Sentry Floodlight Security Camera with Motion Sensor, Intruder Alarm and Audio Video Recording' for review and would like to share my thoughts.

So I have had this camera for a while now and finally got it installed a couple of weeks ago and I am ready to share my thoughts and experience so far. This camera requires hard wiring which is why it took so long to get it installed. In my old home it was going to require me to get an extension cord, drill through my wall in the garage and plug it in, in the garage. This was much more work than I had anticipated. Now the new home already had normal motion sensor lights installed on switches, which made this more feasible for me to install. I took one of the motion sensor lights down and had to retrofit a new mount out of a piece of wood to cover the original hole left by removing the old light. This wasn't to hard to do and the Geeni light mounted with ease. Once installed and I turned the light switch on, it was ready to set up which took some time to do. I had to reset the device several times to get the App to set it up properly which was a quite pain however.

The camera itself is very good but so far I am not happy with all the notifications that I get which seem to be false alerts. It seems that everything seems to trigger this thing with absolutely no control as to how sensitive you would like the sensor to be. This is truly my main con with this device. I ended up turning notifications off on my mobile device which kind of defeats the purpose really.

Then there is the App which has thus far been pretty buggy. It has crashed many times and it is not so easy to find the "actual" activity that it seems to detect. Of all the motion activity that it detects, I would say that only 40% of it is relative. I do have the App set to just record everything (continuous) on the 128gb SD card which makes more sense seeing as there are so many false readings.

As for the good of this Geeni device, the image quality both during daytime and nighttime recording and playback is great. There is very little lag when accessing the footage which is surprising as I have other WiFi cameras that are painfully slow to connect and playback footage. This is probably my favorite feature (when the App doesn't crash).

Overall I do like this motion sensor and think that there is absolute value to it. I am however, really hoping for a firmware update which might help with some of the issues and allow you to adjust the sensitivity of the motion detection. Also it would be nice to have an easier way to track down and view "actual" activity rather than having to try and find that exact moment of capture. It seems to just tag a portion of footage, and you need to watch several minutes before you can find what it detected. You are also able to save the footage via the App, but doing so can take several days for it to show up on your mobile device which is another downside to this device.

I hope that this was helpful.
text_fidelity_b: Geeni Sentry Wi-Fi Wireless Smart Floodlight Security Camera, 2-Way Audio, Motion Sensor Alarm, Audio Video Recording, Works with Alexa and Hey Google

text_fidelity_a:
Victrola Retro Wood Bluetooth FM/AM Radio with Rotary Dial, Espresso I got the "acceptable" unit for total $17 (sorry), one foot pad is missing, I'll innovate. Firstly, I had wanted the chrome front but couldn't afford it and didn't want to wait a week; when I saw this used for the price I just pushed the button.

From the pictures you would think the front is all matte black, it is not. It's actually a very dark brown and the controls are a dark bronze, in shiny metal; closer to chrome aesthetic and looks far better with more tones than the photos would suggest. I'm actually happy I bought the darker color now seeing it. I tried to capture this on my pic, but it's too dark and still doesn't capture the wonderful appearance.

Plugging it in and turning it on was instantly satisfying, easy to use controls, no stiffness, good quality, lights work, radio is a deep amber or orange. Nice wood, looks and operates easily and great.

Tuning to a somewhat hard to get classical station locally was surprisingly easy and the signal came in loud and clear, unlike the other radios I've tried from Amazon. It felt like an old stereo where you didn't have to give it thought and was instinctive in the first 30 seconds without the difficulty and poor reception and static and crackling of tuning and volume controls or pops of turning it on nearly all cheap modern radios have now.

Bluetooth connected and performed seamlessly, perhaps a little softer than the radio but not horribly so. And the sound... On both radio and bluetooth the sound quality is superb; *just* enough bass without being muddy and the treble is good and clear. Bass in the voices and high pitches in the music, and very loud without screech or static at still low volume on the knob, with room-filling sound on FM and bluetooth.

This is the most pleasing product I've purchased from Amazon in a long time, especially in the radio category.

Update: After trying several others, I bought a second one! Like New $21. The only thing I notice is neither sits perfectly evenly, there's a slight wobble, even with all four feet pads. No biggie. Love the radio, excellent big sound, bass, but not muddy. Best radio on Amazon, and a true "table radio".
text_fidelity_b: Victrola Retro Wood Bluetooth FM/AM Radio with Rotary Dial, Espresso

Granted, I've only had mine for a month + 1/2 but this router is very fast and has some cool features. I like the switch on the back to turn off the Wi-Fi and it also has a separate on/off switch for power and, It has 2 USB ports that work very well. It looked a little Greek to me at first, the software, but I got to playing with it and it does exactly what needs to be done. All of our pc's in the house are wired direct Ethernet and the only reason I would use Wi-Fi is for visitors and if and when I buy more devices. The WI-FI on off I see as a definitive advantage. I've had many people in my complex riding my Wi-Fi in the past. If your lazy like me and not real good at setting up networks and security, set up your machines with Ethernet wired connectivity, switch Wi-Fi off and you get full speed to up to 4 or more computers (if you have a network switch more than 4). I have 3 and they all connect to the internet and run very fast, all at the same time. The Wi-Fi on this router is very fast, just take the time to set up security. This router also has all the latest security protocol's.

MINIX Z83-4 Plus 2020 Fanless Mini PC, 4G/64G Intel Cherry Trail Windows 10 Pro [Dual-Band Wi-Fi/GLAN/Dual Output/4K/BT/Auto Power On]. Ideal for Digital Signage, POS and Thin Client Solution. We've been grabbing a few of these mini pcs to test them out and see if they're good for Distance Learning. We have a lot of spare pc peripherals including old school 4:3 screens. But for many, an all in one chromebook or cheap laptop is still infinitely more convenient. But if you do have these accessories laying around, and you're curious how this Minix works for Distance Learning, I'm happy to report it's great! I just reviewed a Beelink mini pc that is very capable too.

The 1080p camera, microphone, speakers and monitor connected with no issues. Windows did all the firmware work. The only software we had to fetch was Logitech's unifying receiver for the keyboard and mouse. In California, many k12 schools are using CLASSLINK and GOOGLE CLASS. I went into my child's account, played around with all the apps. Opened and closed browsers, everything was pretty snappy.

It's mind-boggling that Windows 10 Pro is $200 alone. Of course if you're going to pay full price for Windows 10 pro, you wouldn't put it in a low end computer. Nevertheless, it is awesome that it's included here. I recently reviewed the Beelink T4 which has the Z8500 cpu. On paper, that's slightly a faster cpu, but interestingly, the Z8350 in the Minix is a newer cpu. They may have made the Z8350 more efficient or something. In any case, normal human beings won't be able to tell the difference. LOL! The MINIX Z83-4 Plus is a little bigger than the Beelink T4, but comes with a wifi antennae, and a built in micro SD reader.

Basic activities such as web browsing, watching Netlfix, Youtube, kids doing work on ClassLink, etc., this mini pc is very capable.

SAMSUNG X5 Portable SSD - 2TB - Thunderbolt 3 External SSD (MU-PB2T0B/AM) Gray/Red Samsung X5 External SSD Thunderbolt 3 (500 GB)
This drive is marketed as the fastest External SSD currently on the market. From my testing they are not overstating that claim. I was able to transfer 250Gig of data (using a 2016 MacBook Pro) to the Samsung X5 drive in just over 7 minutes.

The drive uses a magnesium alloy (rather than aluminum) for this case. This means that the drive will not throw off as much heat. Due to this fact the drive has thermal management which will slow the drive down (after extended use) to keep it from over heating. Just be aware of this should you need to move very large files back and forth.

Pros
- Very fast transfer rates
- Comes with Thunderbolt 3 cable
- Solid build quality

Cons
- Expensive. The T5 version is only $109.00 [hence the one star drop. If a tad less expensive, we would have given it the full five stars.]
- Drive may slow down when continually transferring large files due to thermal management.
- Only works with Thunderbolt 3 ports.
text_fidelity_b: SAMSUNG X5 Portable SSD - 2TB - Thunderbolt 3 External SSD (MU-PB2T0B/AM) Gray/Red

After charging the remote and plugging in the wifi dongle, the first thing I did was hit the power button on the remote, intending to turn it on to pair it with the dongle. Nope, the power button shut down my whole computer even as the dongle was starting to download the necessary driver. Once I got the computer, a Windows 10 desktop, restarted, I couldn't tell if the driver had been installed or not. The mouse did not seem to be working at all. The keyboard did produce some results but they seemed to be random. The keys did unexpected, sometimes inexplicable things.

The instructions did give a couple of buttons to push if the remote didn't seem to be paired up. Unfortunately, the print and images were so tiny that I could not decipher what one of the buttons actually was. I tried to find an online manual that might have larger print but couldn't even find the company's website. Randomly pushing buttons finally got the cursor to appear. However, the pointer kept jutting off at odd angles whenever I tried to move the mouse. I managed to decipher the instructions for adjusting the mouse speed but that did nothing to fix the odd angling of the cursor. Moreover, while trying to use the buttons on the mouse side, I again started getting random, unexpected results. The whole thing was a mess and I finally gave up on it all. This product is useless for me. If you are tech savvy enough, you might be able to get it working properly but I'm not going to fiddle around with it anymore myself.

text_fidelity_a:
Toshiba N300 6TB NAS 3.5-Inch Internal Hard Drive - CMR SATA 6 GB/s 7200 RPM 128 MB Cache - HDWN160XZSTA A NAS is a great way to add storage for the whole network where everything can be reached from any system connected. It is not as simple as a USB mass storage device like a thumb drive, of course, but it addresses a completely different issue. So far, this drive has proven to be a good one, though its reliability remains to be demonstrated over the long haul.

I have the 8TB drive, and it is great for dumping huge numbers of videos, music, documents and other media needed across a small network. It is fairly fast too, so streaming video from the NAS to any given device on the network is reasonably smooth as long as the network can handle the bandwidth (keep this detail in mind if you are wanting to stream video over a slower wireless network - the lag isn’t necessarily the drive’s fault). The drive is very quiet, though not silent, and so far seems to stay acceptably cool.

I did learn that it does not work all that well in a USB drive enclosure right out of the packaging. I have an enclosure that is capable of handling drives up to 8TB so I decided to try an experiment with the drive when it first arrived. I put it in the enclosure and connected it to my Windows 10 laptop. The system saw the device, and it even saw the drive and recognized the model and serial number, but it was unable to access the drive or even format it. I had more success with my Linux system which recognized the drive and was able to access the partition table and display drive parameters. I did not repartition the drive or create a file system for my experiment though I believe it would have worked.

Time will tell if this drive will be reliable over the long haul. Based on my experience so far, it has worked out well and I have had no issues. It’s the largest drive I have worked with and can handle a LOT of data. If you need wide open spaces for your network storage solution (or you are willing to fiddle with it to get it working as a USB solution) this is a good choice.
text_fidelity_b: Toshiba N300 6TB NAS 3.5-Inch Internal Hard Drive - CMR SATA 6 GB/s 7200 RPM 128 MB Cache - HDWN160XZSTA

text_fidelity_a:
Fitbit Sense Advanced Smartwatch with Tools for Heart Health, Stress Management & Skin Temperature Trends, White/Gold, One Size (S & L Bands Included) Probably want to select reviews based on "most recent" as that will provide you with most up to date and relevant information pertaining to this product. I acquired my Fitbit Sense in June 2021, it has not yet been a month, but so far so good with 24/7 use. I am slow to check out and use all the features, but what I have interacted with so far has been stellar.

I have been using Fitbit products since April 2015- kinda have a love/hate relationship with this brand. I use the activity tracker constantly, and I greatly enjoy the app. So I have stuck with it as I upgraded over the years (Charge x2, Blaze x2, Versa 2, and now Sense). As with many Fitbit users, there is a known frustration with the products. Despite some of my own qualms, and having the ability to spend whatever I want on any fitness tracker I want, I still end up (so far) with this brand. Mostly because I haven't found a tracker and app that I totally like better. I even have a Garmin, but I find that so far off base of accuracy (save for HR), that it is a glorified watch. Garmin seems to do best for actual intended activities (going for a run, going for a long walk, going cycling) where it seems to not be accurate in steps for any other part of the day (only counts about 1/3 of actual steps unless engaged in a longer duration activity, and even then it takes a few minutes for it to start). Also, the app seems to have a lot of info, but doent really tell me anything. That being said, when it was time for me to buy another fitness tracker--I went from Versa 2 to Garmin.. back to Fitbit. I went with the Sense because the price was right, and it was an upgrade over the Versa 2. After my underwhelming experience with the Garmin, I would have happily taken over a 2nd hand Charge from 2015. At least my steps would be accurate.

Ok, so back to the Sense. WOW, the visual on the screen is really clear and precise. Even way more so over the Versa 2, and I had no issues with that. Set up was EASY, and QUICK. Basically, just like in adding any other fitbit, just let it pair and it will very quickly be all set and ready to go. I didnt have any weird upselling offerings, or at least nothing that wasn't fantastically easy to opt out from. Nothing shady that I saw.

ONE POINT that I DO think is important to know is that if you happen to have a Versa 2 (Not sure if this also happens with regular Versa, Versa Lite, or Versa 3), but this could not be added alongside my Versa 2. I had to take the Versa 2 offline in order to add this Sense. I know this is the case with trying to add more than one of the same products, yet I have always been able to have several Fitbits paired no problem, as long as they were different models. SO, I guess the Fitbit app sees Sense and Versa 2 as the same. Not a big deal as my Versa 2 had essentially died after I wore it on a hot humid day and my sweat killed it (then I brought it back to life after putting it in a bag of rice for about a week, Then afterward the battery was never the same. It drained to nothing daily.. and I needed to not have to worry about daily charging.. hence my picking up a Garmin in the interim to see if I liked them enough to spring for a more fancy model--nope-- and ended up buying the Sense.)

Hope it lasts. I love the look. The band is way better than the old pin style. Swapping out bands is so much quicker, easier, less need for super fine motor skills. LOVE the charger. It just sort of magnetizes to the fitbit. No need to clip in.

SP02 wasn't the main feature I was drawn to, but in order to have accurate use it seems a special clock face is needed, and that clock face will drain battery quicker (from what I have read). That being said,

Battery life has been excellent for me.

Love being able to add other apps, and features. Scrolling is easy, turning face on/off is not complicated.

HEART RATE is accurate. I have tested it against my garmin, two blood pressure devices, and a doctors appointment. All saying the same.

Also, I the voice assistant is great. You can choose GOOGLE Assistant, OR Alexa. This is why selecting most recent reviews on this sort of stuff is important, as the early release of Sense did not have Google Assistant, but would soon with an update. True, and they followed through as I have it.

AT THIS TIME, I have ZERO issues, concerns with this Fitbit Sense. I will be back to update as I learn more, or if I have anything worth sharing that is bad. I keep up with my reviews as needed.
text_fidelity_b: Fitbit Sense Advanced Smartwatch with Tools for Heart Health, Stress Management & Skin Temperature Trends, White/Gold, One Size (S & L Bands Included)

A good comparison is those cables are much like an old car - it should get you there, whereas this cable is like a high end sports car - it will get you there lightning fast, without fail.

This Cat8 is designed to be thin, but don’t let that fool you into thinking that it lacks capacity - within the thin package contains the needed shielding and wires for super fast transfer speeds. The connector bases are reinforced at each end of the wire which really help hold all of the wires in place even if you have to bend and twist it to fit it within the plug. The connector plug itself is gold plated which is the ultimate standard in connectivity.

I used this 10’ cable to run from my router to my NAS - a primary connection where speed and a reliable relay is critical - and I’ve been nothing but impressed by this product.

You will not find a better Ethernet Cable - this is really a top of the line cable that you’ll love. This is a purchase that you’ll never regret.

text_fidelity_a:
Pioneer Active in-Ear Wireless Headphones with Integrated Clip, Red SE-CL5BT(R) At the price (about $40 on Amazon), I expected more from these PIONEER ACTIVE IN-EAR WIRELESS HEADPHONES WITH INTEGRATED CLIP (Red SE-CL5BT(R)). The sound is very clear, which is obviously the most important thing. However, I find the controls (3 tiny, flat buttons) to be fumbly and difficult to use. The fact that the buttons have dual functions (e.g., one button increases the volume when pressed once, and advances music to the next track when pressed and held) is partly to blame. However, the buttons seem slow to respond, so I am constantly pressing and holding when all I want is the press once function.

The headphones paired with both my iPad Pro and my Galaxy S7 smartphone, but NOT particularly easily. To place the headphones in pairing mode, so that your Bluetooth device can see the Pioneer broadcast in the device Settings, you must press and hold the headphones’ center button until a miniscule LED light on the side of the clip blinks alternately red and blue. (Normally, the light is red when the headphones are charging, and slowly-blinking blue when the headphones are turned on and connected.)

What’s hard about that pairing, you may ask? It’s in the instructions, except that the instructions are printed in type so tiny that even the best eyes will need a magnifying glass to read them. Worse yet, the key instructions are printed in pale gray (like grayed-out PC menu selections) on soft, recycled paper that is also gray. Purchasers deserve instructions that are printed in black ink, at the very least.

The clip is nice to have. The battery life isn’t great (about 8 hours), and the battery takes about 2 hours to charge via the included USB cable. The “carrying case” for the extra ear tips (you get size S, M, and L sets) is a small resealable plastic bag. The headphones don’t have “over ear” fit (as stated at least once on the product page), but are strictly “in ear” fit (i.e., battery-powered earbuds).

I didn't try using these earphones to answer telephone calls. However, considering how many mistakes I make with the tiny buttons when playing music, I suspect that I'd be hanging up a lot when I was trying to take calls.
text_fidelity_b: Pioneer Active in-Ear Wireless Headphones with Integrated Clip, Red SE-CL5BT(R)

text_fidelity_a:
OROW S211 New USB-Powered 2.1 Multimedia Speakers System with Subwoofer,16W Computer Speakers,Strong Bass,3.5mm Audio Inputs,Great for PC/PS4/TV (Wooden) First, let me say that I am not an audiophile and have no need for fancy, high-priced speakers and such. For an ordinary listener like me, these speakers had a nice, clear, stereo sound. Both music and special effects in movies or tv shows came through very well. Dialogue in movies sounded a bit flat to me but I wasn't sure if that was the speakers or my ears. When I had the family fifteen year old listen to them though, he thought the dialogue came through just fine. So the issue was my old guy ears, not anything to do with the speakers. All and all, they really do have a nice sound for the price.

To talk about the quality of the speakers' construction, let me make a distinction between cheap and inexpensive. Cheap implies something flimsy that will easily break and fall apart. That's not an issue with these speakers. The materials they are made of are not high-end fancy, but they are not flimsy either. So let's call their construction inexpensive but not cheap.

There were two practical issues though, one trivial, one possibly a bit more problematic. The trivial issue is that the cord which connects the usb plug and speaker jack to your device has a very short connecting wire between the plug and the jack. For a phone or a laptop that is probably a non-issue. With my desktop though, I had to rearrange the usb plugs to open up one close enough to the speaker jack.

The issue which may be more of a hassle is that the volume controls are on the back of the sub-woofer. People usually tuck a sub-woofer away from easy reaching distance. So adjusting the volume may be a nuisance. Personally, I don't know why the volume controls aren't on the speakers which are usually more accessible. This may not be a big deal though if you can control the volume from your device. Just be aware of the possible hassle. In any event, our fifteen year old uses this speaker set to listen to music and movies on his laptop and he is happy with it.
text_fidelity_b: OROW S211 New USB-Powered 2.1 Multimedia Speakers System with Subwoofer,16W Computer Speakers,Strong Bass,3.5mm Audio Inputs,Great for PC/PS4/TV (Wooden)

text_fidelity_a:
DEWALT DXFRS800 2 Watt Heavy Duty Walkie Talkies - Waterproof, Shock Resistant, Long Range & Rechargeable Two-Way Radio with VOX My husband has a lot of use for communication on jobs he has to do in the contracting world. We have had some jobs here at the house which required walkie talkie communication. Let's see how these performed.

WHAT ARE THESE LIKE?
HOW ARE THEY BUILT?
These walkie talkies are tough. They come with the batteries outside of the units, so you have to put them in.

HOW TO PUT BATTERIES IN
You will need a very pointed screwdriver or a small Phillips head screw driver to get the battery cover off. When you screw it back in, it is pretty sturdy.

HOW TO TURN IT ON
The on button on the top is large and easy to cold, dirty, or gloved hands to turn on and off. You can also adjust volume.

CASE?
The case snaps on and off of the units. They stay hooked to the clothes pretty well as long as you are not moving around a lot. In that case, we found them most useful to hold the walkies in the pockets with the clip.

CLARITY OF SOUND?
The clarity of sound was superb. We were doing roof work on the top of a third story and they worked great. We also had to do work about 100 ft away from the point of origin of a wiring job, so we needed that for communication to test the connections. Again, they worked great. Very clear and worked very well.

TOUGH?
These have been dropped a few times and worked very well.

RECHARGING?
The recharging unit has a place for both walkies to be charged. The plug is separate from the base that you charge in. Each receptacle has a red light on it to let you know that the walkie is charging. The plug is small so you can use it on a power strip or in the wall outlet without blocking other outlets. Recharging is fast- within the hour- and they seem to last quite a while before needing to be recharged.

CLIPS
The clips have to be removed prior to charging.

CHANNELS
The different channels we used all worked well. We did not have to use them in a very busy area with multiple walkies, however, so we did not get to test it with a lot of walkie talkie traffic happening on a huge job site.

THE BOTTOM LINE
For a very sturdy set of walkie talkies which charge up quickly and last a long time, these are fantastic for contract work and any jobs that we have had to do. My husband plans to take them to his jobs as well when needed. They have a decent range to them and are easy to operate even with gloves on.

MY RATING
FIVE STARS. We really love these walkie-talkies. They have been fantastic so far for all of the jobs we have had to use them for. I will update if we have anything valuable to add in the future as we continue to use them over time.
text_fidelity_b: DEWALT DXFRS800 2 Watt Heavy Duty Walkie Talkies - Waterproof, Shock Resistant, Long Range & Rechargeable Two-Way Radio with VOX

VANGUARD Endeavor ED 8x42 Binocular, ED Glass, Waterproof/Fogproof, Black (ENDEAVOR ED 8420) This is my third pair of binoculars. Years ago I purchased a pair of Yamaha bincolars for about $200 of a similar power (8 or 10) and diameter (42 or 50) for wildlife viewing. The lens stopped working after two years so I then purchased a fantastic pair of waterproof 10 x 42 Leica binoculars that have served me well on vacation and when I went on safari.

However, these Endeavor ED 8420 binoculars by Vanguard (at the current list price of $339.88) seem to be almost as good as my $1,000 Leica's with the exception that these are not waterproof and the power is only 8 instead of 10. According to the package, it also comes with a lifetime warranty.

The only trouble I had was putting on the carrying strap. The diopter ring was easily set and locks securely once set. The eye cups are easily adjustable. However, because I wear glasses, I had to leave them in the down position. The objective lens cap is fixed onto the binoculars with rubber rings and the eye cap (cover) is hooked onto the carrying strap. This means there are no pieces to lose, which is nice. The body cover has a nice grip to it so the bincoulars are unlikely to fall out of my hands. The weight is 25.8 ounces.

According to the instructions, there is also a tripod adapter which sits between the lens. I honestly don't know if this would work on all tripods after you screw off the cap because of its position and I did not try this feature. A carrying case and lens cloth also is provided.

Although I am not a bincoluar connoisseur by any means, this pair I received for review have impressed me. Time will tell if they last like the Leica's or fail like the Yamaha I had. However, if they fail there's always that lifetime warranty where all that has to be paid is shipping both ways. That's not too bad a deal.
text_fidelity_b: VANGUARD Endeavor ED 8x42 Binocular, ED Glass, Waterproof/Fogproof, Black (ENDEAVOR ED 8420)

MSI Arsenal Gaming AMD Ryzen 1st and 2nd Gen AM4 M.2 USB 3 DDR4 DVI HDMI Crossfire ATX Motherboard (B450 TOMAHAWK) I wanted to build a relatively inexpensive computer to replace my 7-year old machine (also custom built), and after looking at various options I opted for this MSI mobo. I'd used MSI several times in the past, and was happy with their product quality and their support. (BTW, I use pcpartpicker to assemble my components, I recommend the site.)

After putting everything together and running it, I'm very happy with my choice. The mobo physical layout is excellent, installation of the cpu and cooler and graphics card was easy, and all those fiddly connectors were not too hard to identify and access (needed a flashlight sometimes, and younger eyes would have helped). The firmware settings interface is decently designed and easy to use: I particularly liked the fan speed controls.

The Bios flash is easy to do with the firmware file loaded onto a USB key. (I didn't try the funky flash button, did it from the interface.) I wish MSI provided a Windows app to download and update the Bios, as some other brands do, but this is a minor thing.

For the price paid, the value of this mobo is excellent. I highly recommend considering it for a mid-priced Ryzen build.
text_fidelity_b: MSI Arsenal Gaming AMD Ryzen 1st and 2nd Gen AM4 M.2 USB 3 DDR4 DVI HDMI Crossfire ATX Motherboard (B450 TOMAHAWK)

This printer is really handy. It is small, easy to carry, recharges well, and is easy to work. It comes with a USB charging cord, instruction book, and a small roll of paper/film. 10 is the number that came with the one I got.

WHAT IS THE ADVANTAGE OF THIS PRINTER?
Although this is a similar idea to the old Polaroid cameras, the difference with this one is that you get to choose the pictures that you want to print, instead of having to print whatever you take.

DOES IT WORK WELL?
This printer worked great. It is not hard at all to print with and we had no trouble with it.

INSTRUCTION BOOK
The instruction book is easy to follow and use.

QUALITY OF PHOTOS
I am enclosing a photo we took and printed with this printer. It is small and easy to keep handy, but still a great photo to put in a tiny frame as a magnet on the refrigerator, or framed for a small desk area. There are plenty of other things we can do with it, but those are just a few ideas.

WHAT DID WE USE IT FOR?
Our kids went to a pretty big march/event not too long ago and they were able to take a quick photo of them and their friends and print everyone a small copy as a memory to hang on to (especially since 1 of them was not too into tech stuff).

IS IT WORTH IT?
The replacement paper is not cheap, but it is doable if you make sure to keep it handy and only use it for special photos. This only comes with 10 so it is easy to blow through that in one sitting. It is nice to have handy, but only if you use it wisely.

THE BOTTOM LINE
For a good quality instant print photo to help quickly capture a photo you take with your phone in print, this is a nice little printer. It is easy to carry and store, but it does take expense to keep printer paper handy.

MY RATING
FIVE STARS although it is more like four and a half. I would think this would come with a bit more paper to get you started with it, but not enough of a pain to take a star off at this point.
text_fidelity_b: Fujifilm Instax Mini Link Smartphone Printer - Beige Gold

Blink Whole Home Bundle | Video Doorbell System, Outdoor camera, and Mini camera | HD video, motion detection, Works with Alexa I’m 50/50 on the Blink XT2. It’s a decent system that has non contractual usage, which is very awesome... I just find a couple of issues with the system performance. There are no options for notification updates or changes to the system and the only tone that it will play doesn’t not work all me up at night. Also, you can arm the system on a schedule, which is cool, but again system options are limited. I have cameras that surround my house but, my dogs are always setting off the backyard cams... which happens all day and night. You can’t just arm the front yard cameras for all day use while turning off the rear cameras so the dogs don’t set them off in the day time. This means if you’re armed and home, your phone will go off alllllllllll day, and basically be ineffective for monitoring. We have a pool so all day long I’m also going in and out the house and it just adds to the notifications. I hoped this unit would allow more function in settings but it’s just very basic. There are a couple neat Alexa add one, but I refuse to buy Alexa for several reasons and feel there is a ploy to have to buy Alexa when those features like voice announcements or lights turning on upon motion. I like the system for its purpose, but the function and personalization falls flat on its face and that’s the reason it’s not 5 stars. I’ve read posts and there is AMPLE feedback to Blink/Amazon to correct the notifications (again notification ringer is ineffective unless awake and CANNOT BE CHANGED) but isn’t fixed. I have iphone, heard android users have a little more function??? Yet another uncorrected design flaw.

Also, the system crashes from WiFi for no identified reason and requires you to mess with the system. Doesn’t take long but had this a week and happened twice while I’m out and renders the system useless.

Another issue is that there is a 10-15 second delay to speak live through the cameras, even with early detection on. Still helpful, but trying to talk to someone through the cameras, like a delivery guy or unexpected guest, creates a lot of awkward conversations through the system.

Ideally... it works, and will help, but personalization and lack of settings to help your needs of the system can find a lot of improvement and hope these system flaws are improved as they are completely within the ability to improve function of their designs. Had these issues not been present the system would get 5 stars as the cameras are great, the system is very easy to install and get going, adds piece of mind that you otherwise wouldn’t have with out a high dollar monthly contract. All in all, it’s an improvement to safety, but many things can improve to make it effective and useful. Until then, it’s just bland

Sony SRS-XB12 Mini Bluetooth Speaker Loud Extra Bass Portable Wireless Speaker with Bluetooth -Loud Audio for Phone Calls- Small Waterproof and Dustproof Travel Music Speakers Gray SRS-XB12/H [[VIDEOID:bbb3e1079eb39e7b0d0221b2e128e01d]] I am not an audiophile; however, I know great sound when I hear it, and this tiny speaker delivers crisp, clear sound. I would expect nothing less from Sony. However, it is a little bright with more midrange and treble and it sometimes sounds a little thin. The bass has a little bit of thump and does not distort even with the volume maxed out.

I used an audio cable with my Echo Dot and Bluetooth with my phone and computer.

Steely Dan is my test music, and my EQ is set to flat so I can hear what this speaker is capable of without the help of any adjustments.

I made this video using my largest audio file on my MacBook Pro. You can be the judge.

The only things I do not like are the controls, and I think the volume is lacking. I have the volume set to max on both the speaker and my computer. It can fill the small area I am occupying, but not the room.

It's a very compact speaker, and I think it sounds tremendous when you consider its size. The clarity is impressive, and it does not distort. Overall, I am pretty happy with the sound quality and I would have rated it higher if the price point were lower. At the time of this review, it costs $50 and there are a lot of great speakers at nearly half that cost. If it could produce the same sound clarity with more volume it would be worth every penny.
text_fidelity_b: Sony SRS-XB12 Mini Bluetooth Speaker Loud Extra Bass Portable Wireless Speaker with Bluetooth -Loud Audio for Phone Calls- Small Waterproof and Dustproof Travel Music Speakers Gray SRS-XB12/H

text_fidelity_a:
Panasonic HomeHawk Window Home Monitoring Camera for Outdoor Monitoring, Mounts to Inside Window, Color Night Vision, Wide Angle, 24/7 Full HD Recording, Person Detection, Alexa Compatible KX-HNC500 I've used cheap Wyze cameras as well as more expensive cameras like Arlo in my garage, but wi-fi is pretty iffy there. I wanted to see if the wi-fi receiver in this HomeHawk beats the Wyze or Arlo, but unfortunately, that's not the case. The HomeHawk struggled in my garage as much as the others did. As a matter of fact, I couldn't connect to it at all. So right off the bat, that is something to note... that paying more for a camera doesn't necessarily mean better wi-fi receivers are inside the camera. This isn't something I'm going to subtract a star for since no cameras on the market can help with my wi-fi situation, that's something that will have to be remedied by wi-fi extenders.

Now once I move this camera indoor, with better wi-fi reception, to monitor the backyard, it does the job wonderfully! The app is great and full of features. Be sure you select the proper MODE. By default, it was on BASIC and it did not do any recordings. I realize I had to change it to PROTECTION mode or 24/7 mode. Or, better yet, you can create your own mode! You can determine if it will record 24/7, or only when it detects motion. You can determine the duration of the clip. Now that is pretty cool! The default is 10 seconds, and for several weeks I thought I had to live with the default, until I discovered that I can actually change this by creating my own Mode. You can determine if it will notify you for every motion detected, or only for human detections. Lastly, you can name the mode anything you want, then select it and you're set! I've only used Wyze, Arlo and Homehawk cameras, and without a doubt, this Panasonic software is the best of the bunch. 5-stars!
text_fidelity_b: Panasonic HomeHawk Window Home Monitoring Camera for Outdoor Monitoring, Mounts to Inside Window, Color Night Vision, Wide Angle, 24/7 Full HD Recording, Person Detection, Alexa Compatible KX-HNC500

Pogoplug Backup and Sharing Device (Discontinued by Manufacturer) Pros: If you are a beginner to computer networking and you just want to host a cloud server at home for tablet and smartphone access to your music and video library, this is the device for you. Set-up is simple, anyone who can install a Linksys router can do it, and tech support is decent (for the purposes of this review, I called and asked them to help me with a non-existent issue so I could report that they do in fact help people, then I told the guy I was a mystery shopper and thanked him for his help).

Cons: If you have Carbonite back-up service, if you have a WD MyBookLive NAS, or if you know how to configure any of the several dozen software packages that do this for you, then you can already do this for free without buying this device. Yes, I do mean that there are free packages (at least for Android phones) which you can download and use to make your computer into this device without any fees whatsoever. So for anyone who is mid-level or above in computers, this is not a worthwhile purchase.

text_fidelity_a:
REETEC Wireless Bluetooth Headphones Over-Ear - [40 Hrs Playing Time, Soft Protein Earpads] Foldable HiFi Stereo Wireless Headphones with Microphone, Deep Bass Headset for Phone, PC, iPad - Rose Gold I've owned many wireless headphones, so this isn't my first rodeo. I wanted something separate to leave paired with my work computer. Earbuds aren't comfortable for me to wear for long periods of time so over-the-ear style is important. I have to admit, I like these more than I expected to. The ear pads are soft and slow to reclaim their shape like memory foam- this makes them extremely comfortable to wear so I don't mind keeping them on for a good portion of my workday. It also has a rubberized cover for the charging port and 3.5mm jack, which is surprisingly nice to find on a headset in this price range!
The sound quality is about on par with what I expected for this price range- that is, it is very good. Not blow-your-mind-amazing like sets that sell for hundreds, but as good if not better than others in this price range. What I didn't like, however, is the microphone quality. Yes, it has a mic, but I'd like to pretend it doesn't. The mic is on the headset by my ears and doesn't seem to be directed towards my mouth. This makes my voice sound distant and muffled, with ambient background noise sometimes on the same level or louder than my voice is. For calls I'd rather use a different headset, but that's OK. This ends up being used paired with my computer rather than my phone. It is pretty decent at passive noise isolation as well, reducing sound around you naturally. The only things I wish were better are the mic and perhaps a physical on/off switch rather than a button, but honestly this is pretty normal for headphones in this price range so I essentially got exactly what I expected.
EDIT:
I loved these so much, I ended up getting another on in another color for a family member. A great value for wireless headphones.
text_fidelity_b: REETEC Wireless Bluetooth Headphones Over-Ear - [40 Hrs Playing Time, Soft Protein Earpads] Foldable HiFi Stereo Wireless Headphones with Microphone, Deep Bass Headset for Phone, PC, iPad - Rose Gold

text_fidelity_a:
Microsoft Surface Book 13.5" (Intel Core i5, 8GB RAM, 256 GB) So my only complaint about Microsoft devices as a whole is their lack of compatibility with Linux. This one is better than the other 4 I have owned. It still isn't working well with CentOS, but Kubuntu works awesomely, and I also have Kali running. I've got a tripple boot (with Windows as well) set up, and the whole thing took about 5 hours to set up. If you're looking for a laptop to run Linux on, that is light and has a great battery, the choice is this one or the XPS. The XPS (my friend has one) doesn't run touchscreen, but it is lighter than this one and gets even better battery...

Overall, this laptop has a great battery, a great screen, and runs Linux with very little effort. The only downsides are the requirement to have power connected in order to detach the screen (yes, the button does work in Linux), the fact that all ports (USB, SD and charging included) are on the base (so in tablet mode it can't charge, can't read an SD card, and can't use a USB device), and the fact that it is so sealed that you can't upgrade or repair it yourself. Those are the reasons I dropped one star (personally, I'd drop 4 stars for all that, but I know most people wouldn't).
text_fidelity_b: Microsoft Surface Book 13.5" (Intel Core i5, 8GB RAM, 256 GB)

text_fidelity_a:
Osprey Nova Women's Laptop Backpack I walk to school everyday, it's about a 30minute walk. That combined with all the time walking to different buildings once I'm at school, is a lot of time to get cozy with this backpack.

A little back story, I previously owned a unisex North face backpack, I got rid of it because it was too big and hurt my back. I downsized to a women's North face. It was better but it still didn't seem very comfortable and never felt very light even with few items in it.

Cut to this backpack, it's a women's backpack so it's made smaller. (Also I'm 5'7" 120lbs so I'm not terribly small bit still). This backpack feels lighter than others, I think it has to do with the frame, it's very comfortable on. I typically have 2 binders and two medium sized textbooks in my backpack, occasionally I'll bring my laptop. With everything in it, It doesn't irritate my lower back or shoulders after hours of wear.

The backpack also comes with 2 straps on the side that allows you to compress it in even further. When your stuff is closer to your back, and not hanging far out, it's a lot more comfortable. There are several pockets, a large padded pocket for your laptop, another for your books and such and 2 smaller but still very spacious pockets, as well as an interior pocket and nonzippered outer pocket.

The pockets do zip all the way around, but the straps will need to be unbuckled to do this. I'm not gonna lie, I'm very lazy and have not unbuckled the straps since getting this item, (it's been a month), and I've been able to get my books/laptop in and out without a problem.

The pockets for waterbottles are nice and deep so your water bottle won't fall out, and there's also a strap on either side to secure it even further.

The chest strap on this is awesome too. It doesn't compress your chest in an awkward or uncomfortable way which is something I always look for.

The shoulder straps and back are vented so it's been really great for me, a very sweaty person walking in the summer time. Haha

Overall I think this backpack is awesome! I've already recommended it to my school friends, looks like Osprey is my new go to backpack brand!:D
text_fidelity_b: Osprey Nova Women's Laptop Backpack

Netgear WGR614 Wireless-G Router We bought this Netgear WGR614 router back in March 2006. It installed somewhat easily and except for a little problem with the wireless PC card for the laptop (wouldn't be recognized at first but easily corrected) we had pretty stable use for about a year. Then we began to have connection problems. The connection would get slower and slower until internet pages would just not load, resulting in repeated "page cannot be displayed" errors. Powering down and restarting the router, modem and computer seemed to correct the issue. But as of this morning the router appears to have completely died. Powering down and restarting does nothing, the internet connection cannot be re-established. We can connect the desktop directly to the cable modem but for now the laptop is without connection, making for some unhappy family members here.

As of right now I don't know if we'll be buying another Netgear router & wireless PC card. The life expectancy of Netgear products does not appear to be all that great. Looking at some of the reviews we appear to be quite lucky that we got as much time out of the router as we did. Still I'm not in the mood to be shopping for a new router every 1.5 years or less. Hopefully there is a good router out there that can last at least two years.
text_fidelity_b: Netgear WGR614 Wireless-G Router

Led Ring Light 18 Inch Selfie Light Circle Light kit with Tripod Stand, Dimmable 3000K- 6500K Lights for iPhone with Phone Holder, Lighting for Video Recording, Makeup, Live Stream, YouTube Equipment Note: There is more than one product attached to this listing. I am specifically reviewing the 18” light.

One of the things I have been researching for a while is ring lights. I have wanted one for a little while, but not the kind that sits on a desk and is only useful for making personal videos for upload. I wanted one that would be suitable for taking portrait photos and would be suitable for professional use. This is a nice ring light to that end and so far I am pleased with it, though I have not been using it long.

This is a large light, 18” in diameter which makes it quite a bit larger than most ring lights available right now. It is large enough that you can shoot photos or video through it using a full-sized camera with little effort, which is what I was looking for. It comes with a full-sized tripod (which it needs) as well as a nylon carry bag. It also comes with a mounting makeup mirror in the bag which is something I will not use with the ring light (I have other uses for it). In includes all of the hardware you need for mounting your camera, video camera or phone if you are a vlogger or content maker.

The very first thing I did with this light was point my camera right at it while using the electronic shutter, in order to determine if the LEDs in this light are strobing or not. I half expected these to strobe based on the price, but they do not which is a very good thing. It means steady, consistent light that does not flicker.

There are two adjustment knobs that are on the light assembly, one to control the brightness and the other to control the light temperature. The temperature range (speaking in generalized, observable terms rather than technical terms with numbers) allows for setting the light from an orangy golden-hour glow to a piercing frosty blue, and everywhere in between. So, though it may require some messing it allows for getting the light temperature just right based on skin tone and background. The brightness can be varied from a soft glow to bright enough to hurt your eyes when looking right at the ring. Thought not designed for such, this would work as a studio light in a pinch...

I do not have a light meter to check the actual light temperature or the lumens/lux output.

There’s a plastic cover over the LED array that helps to diffuse the lights and make them easier to face when using the light to illuminate a face for portraits.

The power source is AC 110/120. Some ring lights I have seen and used have USB-based power input instead. These tend to be smaller and less powerful.

Construction is good though I would stop short of saying it is solid and rugged. It is mostly plastic so it does have some flex to it but seems sturdy enough to handle getting moved around and jostled some. Because the housing is plastic instead of metal this is a lightweight unit and is easy to transport. This is a trade-off I have seen with tripods as well – lightweight for travel, heavier for less mobile work. This light seems geared for the traveler based on that.

Overall, I am pleased with this light. It is a bit better than I expected and it has everything you need in the package to be suitable for vlogging or studio use. It’s a big light so it does cost a bit more than a lot of the smaller, USB-powered lights out there but the cost is reasonable. If you’re looking for a ring light that can be used for either video content or of portrait work, give this one some consideration.
text_fidelity_b: Led Ring Light 18 Inch Selfie Light Circle Light kit with Tripod Stand, Dimmable 3000K- 6500K Lights for iPhone with Phone Holder, Lighting for Video Recording, Makeup, Live Stream, YouTube Equipment

The sunglasses have enough of a tint to be comfortable, but not so much that they are impractical in low light. I preferred these for comfort and for sound quality to ear buds. The sound quality is about what you'd expect for tiny speakers mounted to the arms of sunglasses. It's not concert hall quality, but it gets the job done, and it's better than a lot of other speakers on the market.

These sunglasses are great for athletes who like to listen to music while they're out exercising. Also included is a case, a bag, a lens cloth, and a charging cable.

Kindle Keyboard 3G, Free 3G + Wi-Fi, 6" E Ink Display - includes Special Offers & Sponsored Screensavers After running out of space for bookcases and space *on* those bookcases, it was suggested that I look into getting an ebook reader. I decided to give a Kindle a try, and it's made the transition from paper to e-ink a mostly painless transition. The Kindle Keyboard is lightweight - even with a cover it's light enough to hold for long periods of time and usually thinner than most books. It's a little bigger than most paperbacks but smaller than hardcovers, to I can fit it into a larger purse and take it with me if I'll have time to kill during any appointments. Of course, it makes traveling much, *much* easier as now I only need to pack the Kindle and one book to read during that 'power off all electrical devices' time.

The 3G version allows more connectivity but does drain the battery faster. If you want to conserve energy, you can turn it off unless you are downloading a book. The keyboard is small, but I haven't found it too tiny to use when unlocking it for use or searching. My only complaint is sometimes trying to remember when to use the 'Menu' button and the 'square' button for some features - it could be a bit more intuitive (like when to remove a book or sample from the device).

The Kindle Keyboard is only 4GB (actually a little less) and can't be expanded beyond that, but it does hold a lot of books. It's also easy to load books by USB cable and sending via email (to Kindle email account). It's definitely saved at least a bookcase or two! While I would hate to see all books go digital, if you do have an issue with space or you want to have a few books always on hand, a Kindle definitely helps in that regard.
text_fidelity_b: Kindle Keyboard 3G, Free 3G + Wi-Fi, 6" E Ink Display - includes Special Offers & Sponsored Screensavers

I'm sold, and would definitely buy again, and would recommend it for anyone taking pictures of miniatures of any kind.

text_fidelity_a:
LotFancy 7 Inch 16:9 TFT Color LCD Widescreen Car Rear View Monitor Bundle with Remote and Waterproof Camera I received this as a free review sample five months ago and have been using it for around four months. This is a rear view monitor only - not a dashcam - and it works far better than one of the combination rear monitors/dashcams that I have also used.

Since there are a large number of reviews that cover this in detail I am going to keep mine brief. Here is the single thing I do not like about it: the terrible documentation. On the other hand you can have this professionally installed for not a lot of money, which is the route that I took. If you are a do-it-yourselfer installing it right is less than an hour job (according to the tech who installed mine).

What I love is the clear visual behind me. The camera works in dark and low light, and the display has sufficient clarity and resolution to easily see what is behind you and estimate distances. If you were to purchase this as an option on a vehicle I shudder to think of the cost, but for less than one hundred fifty bucks professionally installed this is a bargain. And if you do install it yourself you can knock a C-note off that cost.

If you parallel park frequently this is a perfect way to make that easier. For rural driving this may not be a needed accessory, but for city use it's a convenience (and a safety feature as well.) Do note the information in the product specs too because they are clear about what this will and will not work with.
text_fidelity_b: LotFancy 7 Inch 16:9 TFT Color LCD Widescreen Car Rear View Monitor Bundle with Remote and Waterproof Camera

text_fidelity_a:
Brainwavz M1 in-Ear Noise Isolating Earphones I have tested a number of in ear monitors (IEMs) from Brainwavz and other brands and the review sample that I received is the best in its price range that I have come across. In fact, it's best in sub one hundred dollar IEMs.

The best feature to me is comfort because I normally do not care for in ear style phones. I can wear these for hours without even noticing them, and they ship with an array of tips that fit just about any ear size.

However, sound ranks right up there with comfort because I listen to a lot of music from a critical perspective as well as enjoyment. Nothing interferes with the sound quality, including ambient noise from the cables or other physical factors, and they do a great job of isolation. Every album to which I listen comes across with no gaps in any of the frequency bands. You can hear any note (and sometimes flaws) that musicians and recording engineers made, which is extremely important to me.

What truly sets these IEMs apart from other phones in its class are is the attention to detail. The cord is tangle free and practically indestructible. I have yet to worry about breaking or wearing out the inner conductor like I do with some other brands I own (including some pretty expensive phones). The plug is gold plated for and at a ninety degree angle - nice touches - and the phones ship with a protective hard case ([[ASIN:B00HPPL1M4 Brainwavz Hard Earphone Case]]) that is not only convenient, but functional.

If I had to recommend a sub one hundred dollar set of IEMs to a friend or fellow musician these would be it. The performance, comfort and price make them a bargain in my opinion.
text_fidelity_b: Brainwavz M1 in-Ear Noise Isolating Earphones

text_fidelity_a:
Bone Conduction Headphones with Noise Cancelling MIC for Clear Calls, IPX6 Waterproof Open-Ear Bluetooth Wireless Headset for Calling, Running, Bicycling, Hiking (Green) Bone conduction headphones have become quite popular and because of this, there are many to choose from. This specific model is quite minimalist. A thin metal frame with the vibration units and electronics hanging off it.

In terms of comfort, there is no adjustability to the metal frame so it may take some getting used to because the frame may feel like they are too big or too small depending on your head size. For me it felt a little bit loose but I came to realize that it actually stayed where you place it and it really wasn't a problem.

For sound quality, this bone conduction headphone will never match a nice pair of over-ear headphones but that really isn't what it's for. By leaving the ears open, one is still able to stay aware of the surroundings, making it great for cycling and jogging where hearing the traffic is essential for safety reasons.

A pair of earplugs are included with this product and with one or both in, one can really appreciate the difference between regular headphones and bone conduction. You can still hear the music (or in my case, audiobook) through the earplugs because of the bone vibration but all outside sound is cut off. This means that you'd be able to listen to music over the sound of a loud machine.

I have tried a few different pairs of bone conduction headphones and these are the ones that I have stuck with so far. The buttons maybe be somewhat limited (just two buttons that control volume and power), but they are easily reachable and not hard to press and the IPX6 means it's water resistant against rain and sweat.
text_fidelity_b: Bone Conduction Headphones with Noise Cancelling MIC for Clear Calls, IPX6 Waterproof Open-Ear Bluetooth Wireless Headset for Calling, Running, Bicycling, Hiking (Green)

text_fidelity_a:
Sony MDRNC8/WMI Noise Canceling Headphone, White I thought "They're cheap, why not?" I expected that Sony would at least make a semi-descent product, but I was wrong. They only cut out about 5% of ambient noise. I tested them in a lot of different environments and it didn't perform well under any circumstance.

I compared them to a pair of low-end headphones ($20) to set a baseline, see below.

Test:
In flight - no noticeable difference between each pair
While driving - slightly better muffling of midrange noise, but slight (2% better)
Fan on high & low - slightly better canceling of low freq noise (2% better)
In crowed auditorium - slight better muffling (1% better)

They barely did any better than the cheap-o, non-noisecanceling, over the ear headphones I got for half the price.

The biggest thing I noticed is that the very little amount of noise that was actively cancelled was replaced fully by a hissing sound. This made the headset pretty much useless.

I would recommend not buying these headphones. I returned the set I bought, and got my money back. There are better headsets at this price.
text_fidelity_b: Sony MDRNC8/WMI Noise Canceling Headphone, White
